questions.prompt: How does this chapter define intuition?
choices: Understanding deeply before stacking more knowledge
Following vague feelings instead of analysis
Gathering more information as quickly as possible

explanation.gentle: Young uses intuition to mean deeper understanding before more accumulation, not vague instinct.
explanation.direct: A is correct because the chapter defines intuition through depth before build-up.
explanation.competitive: Dig first. Do not keep piling layers onto weak ground.

questions.prompt: Why can adding more material be a mistake in this chapter?
choices: Because shallow understanding can make later learning brittle
Because new material is always harmful
Because repetition should replace all conceptual work

explanation.gentle: The chapter warns that more layers can sit on weak understanding and make future learning less stable.
explanation.direct: A captures the core risk: accumulation can outrun real grasp.
explanation.competitive: More bricks do not help when the structure underneath is shaky.

questions.prompt: Nina can repeat a workflow step, but when the situation changes slightly she no longer knows why the step works. What move best fits the chapter?
choices: Pause new layers and deepen her understanding of the step before adding more complexity
Keep adding new procedures until the confusion sorts itself out
Treat the variation as proof that understanding does not matter

explanation.gentle: The chapter would slow down and strengthen the underlying grasp before more build-up.
explanation.direct: A follows intuition by repairing depth where surface fluency has been exposed.
explanation.competitive: Fix the foundation before stacking another floor.

questions.prompt: What does shallow fluency hide according to this chapter?
choices: A weak understanding that shows up when variation or deeper questions appear
A healthy balance between depth and progress
Proof that more information is no longer needed

explanation.gentle: The chapter says a learner can look smooth on familiar material while deeper understanding is still thin.
explanation.direct: A is right because surface performance can conceal fragile understanding.
explanation.competitive: Smooth motion can hide a weak grip.

questions.prompt: What boundary does the chapter place on depth work?
choices: Depth should reconnect to the real skill instead of drifting into endless abstraction
Depth means delaying practice for as long as possible
Depth only matters in academic subjects

explanation.gentle: Young keeps intuition practical by insisting that deeper understanding must reconnect to actual performance.
explanation.direct: A states the chapter's limit: depth is useful when it changes the skill, not when it wanders away from it.
explanation.competitive: Dig deeper, but stay on the actual site.

questions.prompt: Why is “more information is not always the next right move” central here?
choices: Because later learning depends on the strength of the understanding already underneath it
Because the learner should stop accumulating knowledge entirely
Because intuition means acting without explanation

explanation.gentle: The chapter argues that later learning rests on current understanding, so build-up is weaker when the base is thin.
explanation.direct: A is correct because depth changes what later learning can stand on.
explanation.competitive: If the base is weak, another layer just spreads the problem.

questions.prompt: Omar keeps adding examples to his notes, but he still cannot explain why the method works. Why does that matter here?
choices: It shows accumulation is outrunning understanding
It proves explanation is unnecessary for learning
It means he should avoid all future practice

explanation.gentle: The chapter would treat this as a sign to deepen understanding before adding more material.
explanation.direct: A fits the principle because surface build-up is moving faster than real grasp.
explanation.competitive: He is adding layers to a structure he still cannot read.

questions.prompt: When is a learner most likely mistaking progress for intuition?
choices: When smooth repetition is taken as proof of deep understanding
When the learner tests understanding with variation
When depth work reconnects to real performance

explanation.gentle: The chapter warns that familiar performance can look stronger than the underlying understanding really is.
explanation.direct: A is right because surface fluency can flatter the learner into building too soon.
explanation.competitive: A clean routine can hide weak structure.

questions.prompt: How does deeper understanding improve later learning in this chapter?
choices: It gives later layers a stronger structure to rest on
It removes the need to learn anything new
It replaces practice with pure reflection

explanation.gentle: Depth matters because later learning becomes stronger when it rests on something solid.
explanation.direct: A follows the chapter's logic that build-up depends on the quality of what is already understood.
explanation.competitive: A better base lets the next layer hold.

questions.prompt: Once a learner has deepened understanding instead of only adding more layers, what question naturally comes next?
choices: How to move beyond defaults and experiment with alternatives
How to avoid all future accumulation
How to turn intuition into a mystical feeling
